extracted.intended_audience: writers, screenwriters, students of mythology and narrative structure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for structuring a story using Joseph Campbell's 17-stage monomyth (Departure, Initiation, Return), including Christopher Vogler's 12-step Hollywood adaptation and criteria for what makes a "good" hero-journey story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three Acts: Departure, Initiation, Return
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campbell groups the 17 stages of the monomyth into these three broad acts; use them as the macro-structure for the protagonist's journey.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Call to Adventure
rubrics_metrics.description: Hero faces a problem/challenge in the ordinary world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 1 (Departure). Serves to disrupt the hero's ordinary life and present the inciting incident that sets the story in motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of the Call
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 2 (Departure). Demonstrates the hero's initial hesitation or fear, which can establish stakes, character flaws, or conflicting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supernatural Aid
rubrics_metrics.description: A mentor/guide provides assistance or talisman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 3 (Departure). Introduces an external helper or object that supports the hero; can foreshadow resources or wisdom the hero will draw on.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Crossing of the First Threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Hero leaves ordinary world, commits to journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 4 (Departure). The point of no return where the hero enters the 'special world'—use to mark a clear change in setting and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belly of the Whale
rubrics_metrics.description: Final separation from known world; symbolic death/rebirth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 5 (Departure). Symbolic turning point emphasizing transformation; can be used to show irreversible change or the start of inner transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Road of Trials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 6 (Initiation). Use a sequence of escalating challenges to develop skills, reveal character, and prepare the hero for greater ordeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Meeting with the Goddess
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 7 (Initiation). Can represent emotional reward, insight, or a profound supportive relationship that reveals what the hero truly values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Woman as Temptress
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 8 (Initiation). Symbolic or literal temptations that test the hero's resolve and priorities; useful to highlight vulnerabilities or moral choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atonement with the Father
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 9 (Initiation). A key confrontation (often with a figure representing authority or destiny) that forces the hero to reconcile, accept, or overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apotheosis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 10 (Initiation). Marks a profound inner transformation or enlightenment that raises the hero to a new level of being or consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Ultimate Boon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 11 (Initiation). The objective of the quest is secured—may be literal treasure, knowledge, or a restored order; this must matter to the hero and the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of the Return
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 12 (Return). The hero may hesitate to return to ordinary life, signaling ongoing internal conflict or fear about applying change in their old world.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Magic Flight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 13 (Return). A hurried or dangerous return journey that can provide tension and show consequences of possessing the boon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescue from Without
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 14 (Return). External assistance required for the hero's reintegration—emphasizes interdependence and that the hero cannot simply solo their way back.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Crossing of the Return Threshold
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 15 (Return). The hero must reconcile the wisdom of the special world with the ordinary world; often involves communicating or embodying change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master of Two Worlds
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 16 (Return). The hero attains the ability to function in both the special and ordinary worlds—signals successful integration and maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to Live
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to live in present moment without fear of death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 17 (Return). The final state of maturity where the hero lives freely and without compulsion, having paid the necessary costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christopher Vogler's 12-Step Adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Ordinary World; 2. Call to Adventure; 3. Refusal of the Call; 4. Meeting the Mentor; 5. Crossing the Threshold; 6. Tests/Allies/Enemies; 7. Approach to Inmost Cave; 8. The Ordeal; 9. Reward (Seizing the Sword); 10. The Road Back; 11. Resurrection; 12. Return with the Elixir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A streamlined, Hollywood-friendly condensation of Campbell's monomyth; useful as a practical 12-step template for screenwriters and novelists. Steps map roughly onto Campbell's stages and can be used when a tighter structure is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful transformation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 'Quality Implications': the hero's change must be substantive and clear—internal and/or external growth that affects the arc and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real loss or sacrifice
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows the protagonist faced real loss/sacrifice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 'Quality Implications': stakes should be tangible; the journey must cost the hero something important to make the transformation credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change that matters to others
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the hero changed in a way that matters to others
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 'Quality Implications': the boon or change should have consequences beyond the hero—benefit or impact on community/relationships/world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor archetypal patterns without imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors archetypal patterns without slavishly imitating them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 'Quality Implications': use archetypes and stages as guiding patterns but avoid rote copying; the story should feel fresh and authentic rather than formulaic.
